exercises.name: Quad set
exercises.summary: Isometric thigh activation with towel under the knee

cues.text: Press the back of the knee down into the towel
Hold: thigh tight, toes pulled up
Relax and breathe normally

form.start: Lie on your back with the leg straight and a small rolled towel under the knee.
cues: Tighten the thigh muscle to press the back of the knee down into the towel
Pull the toes toward you
Hold, then release fully
form.breathe: Breathe normally, do not hold your breath.
faults: Lifting the heel instead of pressing the knee down
Tensing the buttock or holding the breath
form.harder: Hold for 5 to 10 seconds, or add a short hold at the end of each rep.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Rolled towel under the knee
supports.why: Gives you something to press the knee into.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

exercises.name: Heel slide
exercises.summary: Knee bend range, lying on back

cues.text: Slide the heel toward the buttock
Pause, kneecap pointing to the ceiling
Slide back slowly, heel stays down
Rest, relax the leg

form.start: Lie on your back with both legs straight.
cues: Slide the heel along the surface toward the buttock
Keep the kneecap pointing at the ceiling
Go only as far as is comfortable, then slide back slowly
form.breathe: Breathe out as the knee bends.
faults: Lifting the heel off the surface
form.easier: Use a towel or sliding board under the heel.
form.harder: Add a short hold at end range, or loop a strap around the foot to assist.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

supports.label: Sandbag beside the foot
supports.why: Stops the leg rolling outward so the kneecap keeps pointing up.

exercises.name: Straight leg raise

cues.text: Tighten the thigh, lift the straight leg
Hold at the height of the bent knee
Lower slowly over 3 seconds
Rest, relax the leg

form.start: Lie on your back with one knee bent and foot flat, the other leg straight.
cues: Tighten the thigh first so the knee is locked straight
Lift the straight leg to the height of the bent knee
Lower slowly over 3 seconds
form.easier: Do quad sets first and lift only a few centimetres.
form.harder: Add an ankle weight, or hold at the top for 5 seconds.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

supports.label: Ankle weight or sandbag on the lower leg (progression)
supports.why: Adds resistance once the plain lift is easy.

exercises.name: Mini squat

cues.text: Hips back, bend the knees to 30 to 45 degrees
Hold: knees over the second toe
Press through the whole foot to stand
Rest, stand tall

form.start: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands on a counter or arms forward.
cues: Send the hips back and bend the knees to about 30 to 45 degrees
Keep the knees in line with the second toe
Press through the whole foot to stand and squeeze the buttocks at the top
form.breathe: Breathe in going down, out coming up.
faults: Leaning forward with a rounded back
form.easier: Hold a counter and use a smaller depth, or squat to a high chair.
form.harder: Increase the depth, slow the tempo, or add a band above the knees.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Wall sit

cues.text: Slide down the wall, knees over the ankles
Hold: back pressed into the wall, keep breathing
Slide back up slowly

form.start: Stand with the back flat on a wall and the feet about 60 cm out, hip-width apart.
cues: Slide down until the knees are at about 45 to 90 degrees
Keep the knees over the ankles, in line with the toes
Press the back gently into the wall and hold
form.breathe: Breathe steadily, never hold your breath.
faults: Knees drifting in front of the toes
Pushing on the thighs with the hands
form.easier: Use a shallower angle and shorter holds (5 to 10 seconds).
form.harder: Go deeper, hold longer, or progress to a single-leg version under physio guidance.

precautions: Not suitable for everyone with knee pain. Physio to screen.
Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Bridge
exercises.summary: Deep glute activation, lying on back

cues.text: Tighten the lower belly, squeeze and lift the hips
Hold: shoulders, hips and knees in a line
Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time
Rest, breathe normally

form.start: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
cues: Gently tighten the lower belly, then squeeze the buttocks
Lift the hips until the shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line
Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time
faults: Arching the lower back at the top
form.easier: Use a smaller lift, or place a pillow between the knees.
form.harder: Hold longer, add a band above the knees, or progress to the single-leg bridge.

precautions: Keep ribs down and avoid arching the lower back.
Postnatal: after a caesarean wait for medical clearance and avoid pulling on the scar.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

supports.label: Pillow or ball between the knees
supports.why: Stops the knees falling apart and wakes up the inner thigh.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.summary: Hip external rotation with feet together, deep glutes and rotators, side-lying

cues.text: Feet together, rotate the top knee open using the buttock
Hold: pelvis does not roll back
Lower slowly with control
Rest

form.start: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent about 45 degrees, feet together and head supported.
cues: Keep the heels together and the pelvis still
Rotate the top knee open like a shell, using the buttock, while the feet stay together
Lower slowly without letting the pelvis roll back
faults: Pulling with the thigh rather than the buttock
form.easier: Use a smaller range with a hand on the pelvis for feedback.
form.harder: Add a band above the knees, or lift the feet slightly off the bed.

precautions: Keep the pelvis still, no rolling backward.
Antenatal: side-lying with a pillow is fine. Avoid lying flat on the back after the first trimester unless advised.

supports.label: Pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in line with the spine.

supports.label: Small towel roll under the waist if it sags
supports.why: Keeps the spine level.

exercises.name: Glute kickback
exercises.summary: Deep glute activation, hands and knees

cues.text: Brace the lower belly, lift the heel to the ceiling
Hold: squeeze the buttock, back still
Lower slowly with control
Rest

form.start: On hands and knees with hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips and the back neutral.
cues: Tighten the lower belly to keep the back still
Lift one leg back with the knee bent to 90 degrees and the sole toward the ceiling
Squeeze the buttock at the top and lower slowly
form.breathe: Breathe out as the leg lifts.
form.easier: Use a smaller lift and touch the knee down between reps.
form.harder: Add an ankle weight or a band around the foot.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Folded towel or pad under the knees
supports.why: Protects the knees and keeps the hips level.

exercises.name: Side-lying straight-leg hip abduction
exercises.summary: Hip abductors (gluteus medius), straight top leg, side-lying

cues.text: Toes forward, lift the top leg 30 to 45 degrees
Hold: hips stay stacked
Lower slowly over 3 seconds
Rest

form.start: Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent for balance and the top leg straight, in line with the body.
cues: Keep the toes pointing forward
Lift the top leg to about 30 to 45 degrees, no higher
Lower slowly and keep the hips stacked
faults: Lifting too high using the lower back
form.easier: Use a smaller range with the leg slightly forward.
form.harder: Add an ankle weight or band, or slow the lowering to 3 seconds.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in line with the spine.

supports.label: Pillow in front for the top arm
supports.why: Stops the trunk rolling forward.

exercises.name: Shoulder pendulum
exercises.summary: Shoulder mobility, leaning on a table

cues.text: Let the arm hang loose, shoulder soft
Sway the body to swing the arm forward
Return to centre, relaxed
Sway the body to swing the arm back

form.start: Lean forward with one hand supported on a table and the other arm hanging relaxed.
cues: Let the arm hang loose and let the body sway to move it
Make small relaxed swings forward and back, then side to side
Keep the shoulder muscles soft
faults: Using the shoulder muscles to swing
form.harder: Add small circles, or a very light weight if cleared by the physio.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Shoulder rotation with band
exercises.summary: Rotator cuff, band at elbow height

cues.text: Elbow tucked on the towel, rotate the forearm out
Hold: shoulder relaxed, no shrug
Return slowly, keep the band tight
Rest

form.start: Stand with a rolled towel between the elbow and the side, elbow bent to 90 degrees and a band in the hand.
cues: Keep the elbow tucked against the towel
Rotate the forearm outward, like opening a door
Return slowly and keep the band tight
faults: Elbow lifting away from the side
form.easier: Use a lighter band or no band.
form.harder: Use a heavier band, slow the return, or progress to side-lying.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Wall slide

cues.text: Press into the wall, slide the forearms up
Hold: blades wrap around the ribs
Slide down slowly
Rest

form.start: Stand facing a wall with the forearms on it, elbows at shoulder height or lower.
cues: Press gently into the wall and slide the forearms upward
Let the shoulder blades wrap around the ribs and keep the shoulders away from the ears
Slide back down slowly
form.breathe: Breathe out as you slide up.
form.easier: Start lower and use a smaller slide.
form.harder: Add a band around the wrists or use a foam roller on the wall.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Serratus punch

cues.text: Punch up: push the shoulder blade forward
Hold, elbow stays straight
Lower slowly until the blade rests flat
Rest

form.start: Lie on your back with one arm straight up toward the ceiling, holding a light weight or nothing.
cues: Punch toward the ceiling by pushing the shoulder blade forward
Keep the elbow straight
Lower slowly until the blade rests flat
form.easier: Use no weight and a smaller range.
form.harder: Add a light dumbbell, slow the lowering, or do it on an incline.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

exercises.name: Wall push-up

cues.text: Bend the elbows, chest toward the wall
Hold: body in a straight line
Push back to the start
Rest

form.start: Stand an arm length from a wall with hands at shoulder height, shoulder-width apart.
cues: Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall with the body in a straight line
Keep the shoulder blades flat against the ribs
Push back to the start
form.breathe: Breathe in going down, out as you push.
form.harder: Step the feet further back, or lower the hands to a counter.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Wall push-up plus
exercises.summary: SA activation, push a little further at the top

cues.text: Bend the elbows, chest toward the wall
Hold, blades flat on the ribs
Push away, arms straight
Plus: push a little further, upper back rounds
Hold: blades spread around the ribs
Return with control

form.start: Begin as the wall push-up, finishing with the arms straight.
cues: At the top, push the wall away a little further so the upper back rounds slightly
Feel the shoulder blades spread around the ribs
Control the return
form.breathe: Breathe out as you push into the plus.
form.harder: Move from the wall to a counter, then to the floor.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Quadruped push-up plus

cues.text: Elbows straight, push the floor away
Hold: upper back rounds, blades spread
Let the blades come together slowly

form.start: On hands and knees with hands under the shoulders and the elbows straight.
cues: Push the floor away so the upper back rounds slightly
Let the shoulder blades slide back together slowly
Keep the elbows locked straight
form.harder: Hold the plus for 5 seconds, or progress to a plank.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Folded towel or pad under the knees
supports.why: Protects the knees and keeps the hips level.

exercises.name: Scapular row

cues.text: Draw the blades back and down, pull the elbows back
Hold: squeeze the blades for 2 seconds
Return slowly, keep the band tight
Rest

form.start: Stand tall holding a band at chest height with the elbows slightly bent.
cues: Gently draw the shoulder blades back and down
Pull the elbows back close to the body
Squeeze the blades together for 2 seconds, then return slowly
form.easier: Use a lighter band and a smaller range.
form.harder: Use a heavier band or a slower tempo.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.name: Isometric neck press

cues.text: Hand on the forehead, head stays still
Press into the hand, keep breathing
Relax

form.start: Sit tall with a hand on the forehead (or the side of the head).
cues: Gently press the head into the hand with no movement
Build the force slowly to about 30 percent effort
Hold, then release slowly
form.harder: Hold up to 10 seconds, or work in other directions.

precautions: Build force gradually, about 30 percent effort. Do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Deep neck flexor nod
exercises.summary: Deep neck stabilisers, lying on back

cues.text: Neck long, make a small nod
Hold: front of the neck stays soft
Release

form.start: Lie on your back with the knees bent and a small towel under the head to keep the neck neutral.
cues: Make a small nod, as if saying yes, sliding the chin down
Keep the front of the neck soft, with no big muscles working
Hold gently, then release
faults: Using the jaw or throat muscles
form.harder: Hold longer, or add a small head lift under physio guidance.

precautions: Gentle effort only. Avoid if neck pain flares or arm symptoms appear.

supports.label: Thin pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the head level with the chin slightly down.

supports.label: Small towel roll under the neck
supports.why: Supports the natural curve of the neck.

exercises.name: Chin tuck

cues.text: Glide the head straight back, chin level
Hold, keep breathing
Release forward

form.start: Stand or sit tall with the eyes level, using a wall behind for feedback if needed.
cues: Glide the head straight back, as if making a gentle double chin
Keep the eyes and chin level with no tilting down
Hold, then release forward
form.harder: Hold longer, or practise against a wall.

precautions: Raise the screen to eye level. Stop with arm symptoms or dizziness.

exercises.name: Pelvic tilt
exercises.summary: Lower back control, lying on back

cues.text: Flatten the lower back by tilting the pelvis
Hold: belly works, not the buttocks
Release to neutral

form.start: Lie on your back with the knees bent, feet flat and the spine in neutral.
cues: Gently flatten the lower back toward the floor by tilting the pelvis
Use the lower belly, not the buttocks or legs
Return to neutral slowly
form.harder: Add a 5-second hold.

precautions: Small, pain-free movement. Stop with leg pain, numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control, and seek urgent care.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

exercises.name: Knee to chest

cues.text: Draw one knee gently toward the chest
Hold: other foot flat, back relaxed
Lower slowly

form.start: Lie on your back with both knees bent.
cues: Draw one knee gently toward the chest with the hands behind the thigh
Keep the other foot flat and the back relaxed
Hold, then lower slowly
faults: Pulling too hard into the back
form.easier: Use a smaller range and support the leg.
form.harder: Bring both knees to the chest if comfortable and cleared.

precautions: Skip if it increases back or leg pain. Take care after hip replacement.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

exercises.name: Hip hinge

cues.text: Hips back, spine long and flat
Hold, knees soft
Squeeze the buttocks to stand tall

form.start: Stand with soft knees and hands on the fronts of the thighs.
cues: Push the hips back as the trunk leans forward
Keep the spine long and flat (a stick along the back helps)
Squeeze the buttocks to stand tall
form.breathe: Breathe in going down, out coming up.
faults: Bending the knees too much (it becomes a squat)
form.easier: Use a smaller range with hands on a counter.
form.harder: Hold a light weight, or progress to a single-leg hinge.

precautions: Keep the back flat and stay within comfort. Reduce depth with sharp back or leg pain.

exercises.name: Dead bug

cues.text: Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly, back flat
Hold, ribs down
Return and switch sides

form.start: Lie on your back with hips and knees at 90 degrees, arms pointing to the ceiling and the lower back gently flat.
cues: Keep the lower back still
Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly toward the floor
Return and switch sides
form.easier: Move only the legs, or only the arms.
form.harder: Add a light weight or a band.

precautions: Keep the lower back flat. If it arches, make the movement smaller.

supports.label: Small pillow under the head
supports.why: Keeps the neck in a neutral, comfortable position.

exercises.name: TA activation (draw-in)

cues.text: Breathe out, draw the lower belly in and up
Hold: keep breathing normally
Release slowly

form.start: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the spine neutral.
cues: Breathe in, then as you breathe out gently draw the lower belly in and up, as if zipping up tight trousers
Keep the breathing normal while holding
Release slowly
faults: Tilting the pelvis or tensing the buttocks
form.harder: Add leg slides, then dead bugs.

precautions: Breathe normally, do not brace or hold your breath.
Postnatal: avoid sit-ups and crunches until a gap between the stomach muscles (diastasis) has been assessed. Watch for doming along the middle.

Relax fully

Hold the lift while breathing normally
Fully relax between lifts
form.harder: Use longer holds, quick lifts, or practise in standing.

cues.text: Draw the ball of the foot toward the heel
Hold: arch domes, toes stay long
Relax

Feel the arch lift into a dome
Hold, then release
form.easier: Practise seated with the foot supported.
form.harder: Progress to standing, then single-leg.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

cues.text: Heel down, scrunch the towel with the toes
Hold the grip
Release, spread the toes

form.start: Sit with the foot flat on a towel.
cues: Scrunch the towel toward you using the toes
Keep the heel down
Release and spread the toes
faults: Using the leg muscles instead of the foot
form.harder: Place a light weight on the towel.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

exercises.summary: Belly and lower ribs, lying on back

cues.text: In through the nose, belly hand rises
Out slowly, belly falls

form.start: Lie on your back with the knees bent, one hand on the belly and one on the chest.
cues: Breathe in slowly through the nose so the belly hand rises
Keep the chest hand still
Breathe out slowly through the mouth so the belly falls
form.breathe: In for 4 seconds, out for 6 seconds.
form.harder: Practise sitting, then standing.

cues.text: In: ribs widen sideways
Out: ribs close slowly

cues: Breathe in and feel the ribs widen sideways under the hands
Keep the shoulders relaxed
Breathe out and feel the ribs close
form.breathe: In for 4 seconds, out for 4 seconds.
form.harder: Add arm movement with the breath.

precautions: Comfortable breaths only. Stop if lightheaded. Useful on low-energy days.

Lips pursed, out slowly for twice as long

form.start: Sit tall with the shoulders relaxed.
cues: Breathe in gently through the nose for 2 to 3 seconds
Purse the lips as if blowing out a candle
Breathe out slowly for about twice as long as the in-breath

Hold gently for 4
Out for 4
Hold for 4

cues: Breathe in for 4
Hold gently for 4
Breathe out for 4, then hold for 4
form.harder: Use longer counts, or close the eyes.

precautions: Keep it gentle. Shorten the holds if you feel lightheaded. Skip breath holds in late pregnancy or if told to avoid them.

exercises.name: Cat-cow

cues.text: In: lift the chest and tailbone (cow)
Out: round the back, tuck the chin (cat)
Return to neutral

form.start: On hands and knees with hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
cues: Breathe in and gently lift the chest and tailbone (cow)
Breathe out and round the back, tucking the chin (cat)
Move slowly, segment by segment
form.breathe: In for cow, out for cat.
form.harder: Add a hold at each end.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

supports.label: Folded towel or pad under the knees

exercises.name: Cobra

cues.text: Press through the hands, lift the chest
Hold: hips down, neck long
Lower slowly

form.start: Lie face down with the hands under the shoulders and the elbows bent.
cues: Press gently through the hands and lift the chest
Keep the hips on the floor and the neck long
Lower slowly
form.breathe: Breathe in as you rise, out as you lower.
form.harder: Straighten the arms further.

precautions: Skip if it increases back or leg pain. Some spine conditions need screening by the physio first.

exercises.name: Child pose
exercises.summary: Hip and spine mobility, sitting back

cues.text: Sit the hips back toward the heels
Hold: arms long, breathe
Come up slowly

form.start: Start on hands and knees.
cues: Sit the hips back toward the heels
Reach the arms long on the floor
Rest the forehead down and breathe
form.easier: Place a pillow between the hips and heels.
form.harder: Walk the hands to one side to stretch the side body.

precautions: Avoid with knee pain or after recent hip or knee surgery unless cleared.

supports.label: Folded towel or pad under the knees
supports.why: Protects the knees and keeps the hips level.

supports.label: Pillow between the hips and heels if the hips do not reach
supports.why: Lets you rest without forcing the stretch.

exercises.name: Sit tall reset

cues.text: Sit back, sit tall on the sit bones
Open the chest, shoulders relaxed, eyes level
Hold the posture
Slouching creeps in: reset again

form.start: Sit at the back of the chair with the feet flat and the hips and knees at 90 degrees.
cues: Sit on the sit bones and lengthen the spine upward
Open the chest and relax the shoulders
Look straight ahead with the screen at eye level
faults: Sitting on the edge of the seat
form.harder: Hold the posture for longer, then add regular movement breaks.

precautions: Adjust screen to eye level and elbows near 90 degrees. Stand up and move each hour.

supports.why: Supports the natural curve of the lower back so you can sit tall.

cues.text: Slide the arms up the wall, ribs down
Hold: back flat, shoulders down
Slide down slowly
Rest

cues: Slide the arms up the wall while keeping the back flat
Keep the ribs down with no arching
Slide down slowly
form.breathe: Breathe out as you slide up.

exercises.name: Sit to stand
exercises.summary: Functional leg strength, from a chair

cues.text: Lean forward, nose over toes
Push through the heels and stand
Stand tall, squeeze the buttocks
Reach back, sit slowly
Rest

form.start: Sit at the front of a firm chair with the feet hip-width apart and slightly back.
cues: Lean forward from the hips (nose over toes)
Push through the heels and stand tall
Reach back and sit slowly with control
form.easier: Use a higher seat, or hands on a support.
form.harder: Use a lower seat, cross the arms, or slow the lowering.

precautions: Use your arms for help if needed. Rest if dizzy.

exercises.summary: Calf strength and balance, at a wall

cues.text: Rise straight up onto the balls of the feet
Hold at the top, ankles straight
Lower slowly over 3 seconds
Rest

Keep the ankles from rolling outward
Lower slowly over 3 seconds

form.harder: Progress to single-leg raises, or use a step edge for more range under physio guidance.

Hold: hips level, standing knee soft
Lower and change legs

Hold, then change legs

Hold: pelvis and shoulders level
Return with control

Hold, then return with control

cues.text: Heel to toe, fingertips on the counter
Eyes on a fixed point, weight even
Stay tall, small sways are fine

cues: Look at a fixed point ahead
Keep the weight evenly on both feet
Use fingertip support only if needed

Hold: knee as straight as comfortable, relax
Lower gently

Hold steadily with no bouncing

cues.text: Lean the hips toward the wall
Hold: back heel down, gentle stretch
Ease back slowly

Hold the stretch steady with no bouncing

Hold: fingers relaxed, no pain
Release slowly

Hold the stretch with no pain

Return to neutral, relax the belly

Move slowly in a small range

Push up through the heels

Push up through the heels

Elbows soft, shoulders relaxed

Lower with bent hips and knees

Return upright

Keep the fingers relaxed
Hold, then release

precautions: Stop with tingling or numbness in the hand. Keep wrists neutral while typing.

Hold: squeeze the front of the thigh
Release slowly

cues.text: Whole foot on the step

Stand tall, hips level
Step down slowly with control

cues: Place the whole foot on the step
Push through the heel of the step leg to stand tall
Lower slowly with control, tapping the other foot lightly
form.breathe: Breathe out as you step up.

Ease back slowly

Draw the belly in, squeeze the buttocks
Keep breathing, do not sag

Squeeze the buttocks
Look at the floor and keep the neck long

form.harder: Hold longer, add shoulder taps, or place the feet on an unstable surface.

Hold: body in one line
Lower with control

Lower slowly

form.harder: Straighten the legs, hold longer, or add a top-leg lift.

precautions: Start with knees bent if too hard. Keep the body in one line. Stop with shoulder or back pain.

exercises.summary: Back of thigh strength, standing at a wall

cues.text: Bend the knee, heel toward the buttock
Keep the thighs side by side
Lower slowly over 3 seconds

cues: Bend one knee, bringing the heel toward the buttock
Keep the thighs side by side so the hip does not swing back
Lower slowly over 3 seconds

faults: Swinging the thigh forward or back
form.easier: Use a smaller range and hold with both hands.
form.harder: Add an ankle weight or band, or slow the tempo.

precautions: Stay within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop and report sharp pain, dizziness, or new swelling.

Return slowly

Take the arms behind you with straight elbows
Open the chest and keep the chin level

form.harder: Clasp the hands behind and lift slightly.
